messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] A Tutorial Source
messages.body_plain:
The wiki page and guide to geomorph have been removed, because they were
difficult to keep updated and the authors felt they were not adding to
providing proper training to the users.

The package´s documentation brochure and help files are quite complete
(or so we hope!) and they should be sufficient to guide you for
implementing GM methods in R. Also, many questions are frequently
answered through this forum, so if in doubt please search the group´s
history. It is very probable that your doubt has been already addressed
by other users. If this is not the case, feel free to use the forum for
specific questions on geomorph: the authors of the package and other
users will do their best to help you.

For a more full training, keep also an open eye for future courses on
using geomorph to implement GM in R.

Antigoni

messages.subject: trying to understand nested.updated function
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I have been working with hierarchical models to explore size and other univariate terms using lmer4 package, which allow me to include as random factor localities with uneven numbers of observations.  Now I want to expand my study testing similar approaches using skull shape as dependent variable. I don´t want to reduce the shape dimension using PCA or regression scores of shape onto size to avoid miss any important information (as mentioned in this group several times). So, my question is, can nested.function deal with the uneven distribution of samples per locality issue?

I run the code below and it seems to work fine. But after read previously related post in this group and the help function of nested.function I am not completely sure if it really can deal with this issue:

>shape_lm<-procD.lm(coord~log(size)+ Temperature/Site,iter=9999,RRPP=T,data=geoall)
>shape_lm<-nested.update(shape_lm, ~Temperature/Site)

- Another question is that for the fixed factor alone I got a not significant correlation, but the interaction between Temperature:Site was significant. I am guessing that I should consider only the result of temperature isolated since I am interested in the general effect of temperature in my sample, is that guessing right?

>summary(shape_lm)

                               Df       SS        MS      Rsq       F       Z Pr(>F)
Temperature           1 0.001116 0.0011159 0.013921  1.1453  0.4541 0.3316
Temperature:Site  14 0.013640 0.0009743 0.170174  1.5353  6.2381  1e-04 ***
Residuals               65 0.041250 0.0006346

Thanks for any help,

Anderson

messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] trying to understand nested.updated function
messages.body_plain:
Dear Anderson,

The nested.update function does not “deal” with imbalance issues.  It merely changes how F statistics are calculated in ANOVA.  I think the question you wish to ask is if despite your imbalance, does the least squares approach used with procD.lm provide reliable estimates?  You can consider this possibility by the following step by step process.

1. Turn your coordinates into PC scores for simplicity, e.g.,

Y <- prcomp(two.d.array(geoall$coord))$x  # Assuming $coord is a 3D array

2. shape_lm<-procD.lm(Y~log(size)+ Temperature/Site,iter=9999,RRPP=T,data=geoall)

3. B <- shape_lm$coefficients; Yhat <- shape_lm$fitted

4. Run lmer, variable by variable, for the first few variables (Y[,1], Y[,2], Y[,3], …), e.g.,

df <- data.frame(Y=Y, Temperature = geoall$Temperature, Site = geoall$Site)

shape_lmer.1 <- lmer(Y[,1] ~ Temperature + (0 + Temperature | Site), data = df)

5. Compare fitted values from lmer to corresponding columns of Yhat, or coefficients to corresponding columns of B.

If values are close, then you probably do not have to worry about biased LS estimates via procD.lm compared to the REML estimates in lmer.  If you are comfortable, then you could use nested.update for appropriate F values.

Mike

messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Colored Plots
messages.body_plain:
Hi Antigoni, Thank you for the reply.

I realized that perhaps the reason the plots didn't seem correct to me is because they were 2d plots. By trying to extract the scores of plotTangentSpace, I am essentially extracting scores of a 3d data set in shape space and was only using the x and y axes in my plot code above ($PC1, $PC2), which must have given me a plot that was not including the z axis. Is my intuition correct? This would make much more sense, and I presume that my next step would be to use a code in the plot3d package. If this is the case, which function in that package should I directly go to?

-Eddie

On Tuesday, May 29, 2018 at 7:45:57 AM UTC-4, Antigoni Kaliontzopoulou wrote:

> Hi Eddie,
>
> as you say there are many ways to solve this, but I think the easiest in your case is to grab the PCscores from your plotTangentSpace object, i.e. out.pca$pc.scores and then use the same approach you already used before.
>
> Hope this helps
>
> All the best,
>
> Antigoni
>
> On 29/05/2018 03:15, lostle...@gmail.com wrote:

> > Hey all, I'm looking for some tips on how to make a colored plot for a certain data set I have. I have previously made colored plots and respective legends before with other data sets, but I'm having a bit of trouble trying to execute my previous script with data I've used for a gpagen.
> >
> > For context, my previous colored plot script was as follows: I converted my excel tables into csv files and read them into R, then used prcomp to do PCA analyses. I then took the scores of the analyses (mydata$x), wrote them to csv files, and read those files into R again, assigning them to objects. I used RColorBrewer package next to make color palette vectors to assign colors to the species I labeled in my files, and also used pch to assign symbols for Male and Female specimens. Finally, I plotted, using the code below.
> >
> > > plot(PCAnmdScores$PC1, PCAnmdScores$PC2, col=cols_speciesnmd, main="Principal Component Analysis", xlab = "PC1", ylab="PC2")
> > > legend("topright",legend=paste(c("N_beng","N_cou","N_mena","N_kay","N_pyg","N_java"),times=1),col=cols,pch=1,bty="n",ncol=1,cex=0.7,pt.cex=0.7)
> >
> > The coloring I want to do this time is to get colored bubbles for my plotTangentSpace results on some landmark digitized data, but since that's proven to be challenging for me so far, and because I know there are other ways to approach one answer, I figured I can somehow extract a set of scores from somewhere in my data (perhaps from my filelist of landmark data in my gpagen or from a PCA analysis on that array). However, the plots I've gotten don't seem to be right. Maybe someone can help direct me to the right set of scores in my data that I'm supposed to be extracting? Or maybe I'm missing a step? Here is a nutshell of a script:
> >
> > > library(geomorph)
> > > setwd("~/R/.ply and .nts files")
> > > Sliders23<-matrix(c(1,15,2,3,16,4,3,17,5,4,18,6,7,19,8,9,20,11,10,21,12,11,22,13,13,23,14),ncol=3,byrow=TRUE)
> > > all.nts <- list.files(pattern="\\.[Nn][Tt][Ss]$")
> > > all.data <- readmulti.nts(all.nts)
> > > gpa.coords <- gpagen(all.data, curves = Sliders23)                         (My all.data filelist of landmark data doesn't seem to have been the answer)
> > > Links23<-matrix(c(1,15, 15,2, 1,2, 3,16, 16,4, 4,18, 18,6, 5,6, 5,7, 6,8, 7,19, 19,8, 9,10, 9,20, 20,11, 10,21, 21,12, 12,23, 23,14, 14,13, 13,22, 22,11), ncol=2, byrow=T)
> > > plotAllSpecimens(gpa.coords$coords, links = Links23)
> > > plotTangentSpace(gpa.coords$coords)            (This is what I am trying to achieve a colored plot for)
> > > out.pca <- plotTangentSpace(gpa.coords$coords,label = TRUE)                  (Here I used the $scores of my out.pca and wrote them to a csv file, and later even tried a prcomp, but I think I was just totally on the wrong track here with this).
> >
> > The rest of this script, I'm sure, is pretty much incorrect:
> >
> > > pcsv <- read.csv("ppc.scores.csv")             (ppc.scores is a renaming of my out.pca, alldatacsv is my all.data filelist)
> > > cols_pcsv <- cols[pcsv$Species]
> > > plot(pcsv$PC1, alldatacsv$PC2, col=cols_pcsv, main="Principal Component Analysis", xlab = "PC1", ylab="PC2")
> > > plot(pcsv$PC1, alldatacsv$PC2, col=cols_pcsv, main="Principal Component Analysis", xlab = "PC1", ylab="PC2")
> >
> > Any ideas on how to build a code that will help me achieve my desired results?
> >
> > Thank you!
> >
> > -Eddie
